name: Titawin
description: A star 13 parsecs away, 1.6 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 7513: radius 1.571 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 3.345 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.04) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 7513: effective temperature 6232 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.027)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 7513: distance 13.492 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.003), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 13 parsecs away, 1.6 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 3.345 times the Sun's luminosity at 6,232 K, so 1.571 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 7513: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Upsilon Andromedae
quotes.card: Upsilon Andromedae is a binary star located 44 light-years from Earth in the constellation of Andromeda.
quotes.introduction: The system consists of an F-type main-sequence star and a smaller red dwarf.
